answer: No, you don't need a paper lien release. Texas uses electronic titles, so your lender sends the lien release to the state electronically, and we transfer the title electronically at your appointment. If the title record still shows the bank as lienholder, the release hasn't gone through yet. If you can't get your lender to release it, you can sign the lien release request (form NW-LRL-1), and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. While you wait, we can still make you an offer and book your appointment.
